On Mon, Mar 29, 2026 at 09:20 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding ZenPharm report — seeing elevated 429 rates from hosted inference.

Quick update from SRE: we're observing a surge from a small number of high-concurrency clients in the us-west-2 cluster that exhausted available token throughput on a few serving nodes, triggering request throttling (internal rate-limiter). Autoscaling kicked in but had a ~120s warm-up for new pods; in the interim the runtime returned 429s for requests queued beyond capacity.

Mitigations applied at 09:30 PT:
- Increased burst capacity on affected pool (temporary capacity shift)
- Adjusted rate-limiter thresholds for public tenants to smooth short spikes
- Enabled prefix-KV cache on the popular model family to reduce per-request workload

I'm continuing to monitor; error rate dropped from ~25% to ~2% over the next 10 minutes. We'll keep ZenPharm updated and publish a status page message. Full incident ticket: JIRA-RW-4567.

-Markus

Sonia / ZenPharm team —

Following up with the postmortem draft for the hosted inference throttling event yesterday. Summary highlights:
- Impact: transient 429 responses affecting ~25% of requests to token-generation endpoints over a ~25 minute window (09:05–09:30 PT)
- Root cause: capacity exhaustion on a subset of us-west-2 serving nodes due to unexpected concurrency spike + conservative rate-limiter defaults
- Immediate mitigations: temporary burst capacity, rate-limiter threshold adjustment, enabled prefix-KV caching for the impacted model family
- Long-term actions (owner): tune autoscale warm-up (Infra), set adaptive rate-limiter per-tenant (Runtime), default KV caching for model family (Product) — timelines in the doc

Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/RW-2026-03-29/postmortem-draft
JIRA ticket: JIRA-RW-4567

We'll finalize the postmortem and share a customer-facing summary tomorrow. Please let me know if you'd like a quick sync with Markus and our Infra lead.
